messages:
lee: CI is red on linux-amd64 after the morning toolchain roll. Release build of the auth service is failing to link, looks like relocation / PIC issues. Full build command and snippet below, can someone quick-triage?

lee: ```
# bazel build -c opt --config=linux_x86_64 //services/auth:auth_server
ERROR: /workspace/...: Linking of rule '//services/auth:auth_server' failed (Exit 1)
/usr/bin/ld: /opt/toolchain/lib/libstdc++.a: relocation R_X86_64_32S against ".rodata" can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

alex: thanks. Which exact target is failing and is it only on the linux-amd64 shard? any flakes? :thinking_face:

lee: target is //services/auth:auth_server (sorry earlier typo). It repros deterministically on linux-amd64-3 and locally in a container built from the new base image. Not flaky.

jonathan: we rolled the base image + gcc version this morning (gcc 11.3 -> 12.2). Sounds like the static libstdc++ in the image isn't built with -fPIC anymore. I'll kick a CI rerun and do a bisect on the infra image pins. @sre-bot can you rerun linux-amd64-3?

sre-bot: Rerun queued for linux-amd64-3 (build #2247).

maria: I can run a git bisect across infra/docker/base/Dockerfile changes to narrow which commit introduced the bad static lib. Lee, can you paste the local reproducer commit hashes (good/bad) to start the bisect?

lee: reproduced locally on commit abcdef1 (old image) and 1234567 (post-roll). Bisect steps I used: ```
git checkout main
git bisect start 1234567 abcdef1
# run in container: scripts/ci/build.sh //services/auth:auth_server
```
Handing off to maria to run automated bisect.

maria: running bisect now, will report first bad commit.

maria: bisect result: first bad commit is 9b8c7d6 — "bump base image: ubuntu:22.04 + gcc-12". That change introduced a stage that copies a prebuilt libstdc++.a that doesn't have -fPIC.

alex: good catch. Two short-term options: 1) rebuild the static runtime with -fPIC, or 2) switch linking to dynamic libstdc++ so shared objects don't pull the static archive. The immediate mitigation is to pin the infra image back to the previous tag.

lee: can infra pin be done quickly? If so we'll rerun the failing CI against the pinned image while we prepare a proper fix.

jonathan: yep, I can pin the dedicated linux workers to the previous image tag and trigger a manual run. Creating a blocker on the infra board and starting a manual job now.

sre-bot: Manual job started: linux-amd64-3 (manual) #2248. Status: running.

lee: thanks. I'm opening a PR to either revert the bump or fix the build step to compile libstdc++ with -fPIC. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432 (WIP).

maria: I pushed a small CMake tweak to add -fPIC to static targets in services/auth as a stopgap: https://github.com/redwood-inference/services/pull/789 — please review.

alex: lgtm for the stopgap, but prefer fixing the base image properly.

lee: tagging @platform-team for visibility. :eyes:

jonathan: pinned images and manual run succeeded, CI green on the retried shard. We still need the infra PR merged this afternoon.

lee: awesome, thanks everyone. Closing the urgent loop, will watch the infra PR and remove the stopgap after the image is fixed. :thumbsup:
